title: The Job Market
headline_read: The job market is cooling — still solid, but losing momentum.

indicators.title: Unemployment Rate
indicators.context: The share of the labor force without a job and actively looking — the single most-watched gauge of labor-market health.
indicators.read: Unemployment is steady at 4.2%, near its recent lows.

indicators.title: Nonfarm Payrolls · monthly change
indicators.context: How many jobs U.S. employers added (or cut) last month — the headline number markets and the Fed react to most.
indicators.read: Employers added just 57,000 jobs last month — hiring has slowed sharply.

indicators.title: Job Openings (JOLTS)
indicators.context: The number of unfilled positions employers are trying to hire for — a direct read on how strong labor demand is.
indicators.read: 7.6 million open jobs, holding roughly steady.

indicators.title: Wage Growth · year-over-year
indicators.context: How fast average hourly pay is rising versus a year ago. When it outpaces inflation, workers' buying power grows.
indicators.read: Pay is up 3.5% from a year ago, running ahead of recent inflation.

indicators.title: Labor-Force Participation Rate
indicators.context: The share of working-age adults either working or looking for work — how many people are in the labor force at all.
indicators.read: Labor-force participation is 61.5%, down 0.8 points from a year ago.
indicators.no_severity_reason: This level drifts with demographics — the job-market verdict is carried by unemployment, payrolls, and job openings.
